headline: Precious metals drop while natural gas surges and oil diverges
paragraphs: Platinum recorded the day's sharpest loss, tumbling 5.21% to EUR 1,310.06 ($1,467.20) and breaching the $1,500 level, although a specific catalyst remains unclear. Silver followed with a 3.61% drop to EUR 46.01 ($51.52), driven down by persistent risks of a US Federal Reserve interest rate hike and weakening physical demand.

Natural gas rallied 2.95% to EUR 2.59 ($2.90), extending a 9.85% weekly gain on mounting supply risks. Palladium slid 2.17% to EUR 881.74 ($987.50), breaking below the $1,000 threshold, though specific daily drivers were unclear.

In crude markets, WTI rose 1.62% to EUR 93.26 ($104.45) as attacks on Saudi Arabia and ongoing US-Iran tensions stoked supply concerns. In contrast, Brent fell 1.60% to EUR 101.32 ($113.47) as the European Union pushed for accelerated emergency oil reserve releases ahead of winter.
